_doc: The bodies dpay's own OpenCryptoPay checkout puts on the wire (crates/dpay-relay/src/checkout.rs), recorded from the relay's real HTTP surface for the one charge described by `input`, and the SINGLE statement of those bodies anywhere in the tree. It exists because the two halves of this seam cannot be driven against each other: the payer refuses any provider URL that is not https (app/services/opencryptopay.ts) while the offline harness serves the relay at http://127.0.0.1, so no end-to-end run can carry a body from the provider to the parser without weakening a real security property. Both sides read THIS file instead — the provider half is `checkout_wire_matches_the_golden_the_payer_parses` in crates/dpay-relay/tests/relay.rs (drives the routes with `input`, then substitutes every value the provider mints fresh on every call — the payment-link id, the quote id, the per-charge `ref`, the two expiry instants and the charge's own clock — each checked against the shape and the derivation its pinned counterpart states, before comparing), and the payer half is app/__tests__/checkoutWire.test.ts (runs dpay's own parsers over these bodies). Change the wire on either side and both go red. `amount_raw` is the one fact no body carries: the raw VCHF units the decimal amount means, which is what the payer's converter must land on and what credits the sale. `input` is a COMPLETE SIGNED CHARGE-OPEN — the worked example a merchant integrating against this checkout copies — and the relay test verifies its signature with dpay_core::validate_checkout_open at its own `issued_at`. It is not replayed to drive the routes and cannot be: a merchant's signature is single-use and good only within ±CHECKOUT_OPEN_MAX_SKEW_SECS, so a committed one is stale the moment it is committed. The bodies below were therefore recorded from a fresh signature by `merchant_secret` (a throwaway test key that lives here so the recording is reproducible), which is exactly what the test does. Same convention as dfx/catalog_truth.json — a committed cross-language pin, regenerated by driving the running relay when the wire deliberately changes, never hand-edited to make a test pass.

callback.hint: Transfer the exact amount to the address in the URI, carrying `ref` as the transfer's memo, then report the transaction. Reporting is idempotent: if it fails, retry - the payment is confirmed by reading the ledger, not by this call.
